prompt: 54 yo F with long-standing rheumatoid arthritis on chronic hydroxychloroquine, presents with new-onset atrial fibrillation (HR 112, BP 130/74). She has non-insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus, recently started fluconazole 200 mg/day for oral candidiasis. Cardiologist recommends starting amiodarone 400 mg daily for rhythm control—ok to proceed with new amiodarone prescription?

rubric_items.text: Explicitly recognizes the additive risk of QT prolongation and torsades de pointes from hydroxychloroquine, fluconazole, and amiodarone, especially as CYP inhibition increases drug levels.

Recommends against starting amiodarone until fluconazole is stopped (and/or hydroxychloroquine is discontinued or alternatives are found), and suggests alternative rate- or rhythm-control agents without QT risk (e.g., a beta-blocker, with cardioversion considered if appropriate).
Recommends avoiding the combination; if coadministration is clinically unavoidable, recommends specialist-supervised management with baseline and follow-up ECG/QTc monitoring.
Recommends proceeding with amiodarone while continuing hydroxychloroquine and fluconazole without addressing their additive QT-prolongation and torsades risk.
Recommends checking potassium and magnesium and correcting deficiencies before any unavoidable use of this QT-prolonging combination.
